## How the guide defines it

Not addressed in guide.

## How the guide uses it

On 29 pages, always in the informal sense of a team being due to move back toward its underlying quality. John McKechnie expects regression at Texas A&M because things broke the Aggies' way repeatedly in 2025; Makinen says he has become much better at identifying teams due for struggles, which is the same idea stated as a skill.

## Working definition — TTW DERIVED

The tendency for unsustainable results — driven by turnovers, close-game records or scheduling luck — to move back toward what a team's underlying performance supports.

## Why it matters — TTW DERIVED

It is the guide's main argument for fading a good record, and it underpins the Unders bias Makinen states outright on p. 22.

## How bettors use it in this guide

Qualitatively. The guide identifies the mechanism — turnover margin, one-score games, an easy slate — and argues from it, but prints no regression model and no expected-value calculation.

pp. 22–27 where the Unders rest on it; pp. 40–44 for the decline systems that formalise part of it.

## Caution

'Regression' in this guide never means the statistical technique. It always means reversion toward a mean, and no fitted model appears anywhere in the book.
